newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tabcorp says qtr turnover up 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tabcorp says qtr turnover up 17 pct.

text.p: Wagering and gaming group Tabcorp Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday total turnover was up 17 percent in the first quarter of the 1996/97 financial year, despite an "abysmal" start to year from the wagering division.
"The first quarter is up about 17 percent on turnover. Wagering is slightly down and gaming is up," Tabcorp managing director Ross Wilson told reporters after the annual meeting.
Wilson described the wagering division start to the current fiscal year ending June 30, 1997 as abysmal, due to an unusally high number of cancellations.
"We have had a terrible start. So far the weather conditions have absolutely abysmal and we have had just on 23 race meetings abandoned," Wilson told sharesholders.

Wilson saw a slight recovery in the current quarter with an increase in betting turnover on this month's Caulfield Cup horse race meeting, but he said the company was praying for good weather for next Tuesday's Melbourne Cup horse race meeting.
"We are all down on our knees and praying for good weather on Tuesday," Wilson said.

Wilson referred to Tabcorp's recent agreement to pay an increased fee to racing broadcaster Sky Television and said the deal would cost Tabcorp A$700,000 after tax each year. But Wilson said this amount would be offset by further cost cutting.
At 12.25 p.m. (0125 GMT), Tabcorp shares were two cents down A$5.88.
